AMALFI VILLAGE PIAZZA EDGE — Amalfi town piazza edge with ceramic-majolica-tiled street signs, yellow-and-burnt-orange painted houses stacked up the cliff, climbing-bougainvillea cascade burying the lower facades, blue-domed bell-tower above.

PRAGUE MEDIEVAL QUARTER LANE — Prague Malá Strana medieval lane between Baroque-and-Gothic plaster houses in faded rose and amber, climbing ivy and bloom-vine burying the lower stories, iron street-lamp, worn granite paving.

UMBRIAN HILL-VILLAGE LANE — Assisi Umbrian hill-village stone lane between medieval limestone houses, worn Roman-era paving, cascading red geraniums from every shutter, ancient stone-corbelled arches as part of the streetscape above.

SANTA FE ADOBE ALLEY — Santa Fe Old Town adobe street with sun-baked pink-tan mud-plaster walls, turquoise-painted vigas and lintels, climbing bougainvillea and desert-rose consuming low adobe walls, dappled shadow from cottonwood branches above.

MARRAKECH RIAD COURTYARD ALLEY — Marrakech medina alley outside a riad wall with deep terracotta-red plaster above a band of geometric zellige tile, bloom-cascade spilling over the high wall top, carved plaster frieze visible, worn clay-tile pavement.

UDAIPUR PALACE-TOWN LANE — Udaipur old-city lane with whitewashed haveli facades and carved-marble jali window screens, vivid marigold-orange blossom cascade from upper-story terraces, blue-painted doorways half-obscured by bloom, worn stone pavement.

AMSTERDAM CANAL-HOUSE STREET — Amsterdam Grachtengordel canal street with tall narrow brick gable-houses in dark red and brown, bloom-cascade from every sill and window-box across four stories, bicycles absent, stone quayside and mirror-flat canal water reflecting the flower-consumed facades.

MONTMARTRE STAIRWAY PARIS — Montmartre hillside stairway climbing between narrow pale-plaster Parisian buildings, wrought-iron railings consumed by trailing ivy and climbing white roses, a single gas-style street-lamp at the mid-landing, chalk-pale limestone walls softened by bloom overgrowth.

BRUGES CANAL GABLE STREET — Bruges stepped-gable brick facades reflected in still canal water, swans gliding below bloom-heavy window-boxes, weathered red-and-grey brick surfaces threaded with climbing white roses, cobblestone canal-edge path, overcast northern light making every color luminous.

GERMAN HALF-TIMBER TOWN SQUARE — Rothenburg-ob-der-Tauber half-timber Fachwerk facades with exposed dark-oak beams and cream infill panels, window-box blooms cascading from every sill on three stories, cobblestone market-square pavement, a carved-wood guild sign half-consumed by climbing rose.

LUANG PRABANG FRENCH-COLONIAL LANE — Luang Prabang lane with faded French-colonial shuttered townhouses in pale yellow and ivory, Buddhist temple saffron-wall glimpsed at the lane's end, climbing-bloom vines in white and blush-pink consuming the colonial balcony railings, terracotta tile roofline above.

PARIS MARAIS COBBLESTONE ALLEY — narrow Marais alley with cream-stone medieval facades, iron torch-brackets and carved lintels, climbing wisteria consuming the upper stories in purple-violet cloud, cobblestones slick with morning damp below.

PORTO AZULEJO STAIRCASE STREET — steep Porto staircase flanked by azulejo-tile-fronted houses in cobalt-and-white floral patterns, climbing roses threading between the tile-panels, brass lampposts catching late-afternoon gold, sun-bleached plaster crumbling at the edges.

BERGEN BRYGGEN WHARF STREET — Bergen Bryggen wharf row with tall narrow timber-plank houses in ochre, red, and sienna, bloom-vine clusters at every gable window, reflected house-colors shimmering in the harbor water, weathered wooden quay planks below.

BRUGES CANAL-EDGE ROW — Bruges canal-edge with stepped-gable brick houses reflected in dark still water, swans below, cascading bloom-vines spilling from every shuttered window, weathered red-and-grey brick facades half-consumed by climbing roses and ivy.

LUANG PRABANG COLONIAL-LANNA STREET — Luang Prabang street with French-colonial shuttered facades beside golden temple-wall, orange-tiled monastery roof visible above, trailing bougainvillea and frangipani bloom-cascades consuming the colonial plasterwork, worn terracotta-tile sidewalk below.

LISBON ALFAMA AZULEJO STAIRCASE — steep Lisbon staircase climbing between azulejo-tile-fronted houses, intricate blue-and-white geometric tile patterns half-consumed by climbing jasmine vines, a tarnished brass street-lamp overhead, sun-bleached white plaster crumbling at the edges.

HAUSSMANN PARIS BOULEVARD — narrow Parisian Haussmann cream-limestone street with iron Juliet balconies stacked tier upon tier, bloom-cascades of white and lavender wisteria from every wrought-iron railing, wet cobblestones below, mansard zinc rooftops just visible above the bloom-draped upper story.

UMBRIAN MEDIEVAL VILLAGE ALLEY — Umbrian medieval-village stone alley with rough pale-limestone walls, ancient wooden doorways set deep in thick masonry, climbing wisteria consuming the entire upper wall surface in dense purple-bloom clusters, stone-paved alley descending in worn shallow steps below.
